forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329110006_654a633e
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r, j be integers with 0 <= a <= b, r >= 0, and 0 <= j <= floor(r (b - a) / 2). Put I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}. For each positive integer d, define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|, and assume M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d. Let X_j be the set of pairs (S, lambda) such that S is a subset of I, lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I, |lambda| denotes the sum of the elements of lambda, and |lambda| + sum_{s in S} (r + s) = j. Then there exists an involution iota_j : X_j -> X_j such that: (1) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S',lambda') != (S,lambda), then |S'| is congruent to |S| + 1 modulo 2; and (2) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S,lambda), then |S| is even.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329092547_6a64d34a
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate, define (q;q)_n := product_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j) for n >= 0 with (q;q)_0 := 1, set R_{a,b,r}(q) := ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b), and define D := r (b - a). Assume that R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q]. Then for every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), the coefficient of q^j in R_{a,b,r}(q) is a nonnegative integer.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329074016_d9949d95
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with empty product equal to 1. Assume that for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d). Then P_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial in Z[q], and every coefficient of P_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative.

payload.statement_nl:
Let a, b, r, j be integers with 0 <= a <= b, r >= 0, and j >= 0. Set I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}. Define X_j to be the set of all pairs (S, lambda) such that S is a subset of I, lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I, and wt(lambda) + sum_{s in S}(r+s) = j, where wt(lambda) denotes the sum of the elements of lambda. Then
[q^j] product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)) = sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j} (-1)^{|S|},
where |S| is the cardinality of S.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Let
F(q) := product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)) = product_{s in I} ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)).
We interpret [q^j] in the formal power series ring Z[[q]]. This is legitimate because every s in I satisfies s >= a+1 >= 1.

For each s in I,
(1 - q^s)^(-1) = sum_{m>=0} q^(ms)
in Z[[q]], since multiplying the right-hand side by 1 - q^s gives 1. Hence
product_{s in I} (1 - q^s)^(-1) = product_{s in I} sum_{m_s>=0} q^(m_s s).
Because I is finite, expanding this finite product gives
product_{s in I} (1 - q^s)^(-1) = sum_{(m_s)_{s in I}} q^(sum_{s in I} m_s s),
where the sum runs over all tuples of nonnegative integers (m_s) indexed by I.

Likewise,
product_{s in I} (1 - q^(r+s))
= sum_{S subseteq I} product_{s in S} (-q^(r+s))
= sum_{S subseteq I} (-1)^{|S|} q^(sum_{s in S} (r+s)).

Multiplying the two expansions, we obtain in Z[[q]]
F(q) = sum_{S subseteq I} sum_{(m_s)_{s in I}} (-1)^{|S|} q^( sum_{s in S}(r+s) + sum_{s in I} m_s s ).

Now fix j >= 0. Only finitely many terms on the right can contribute to the coefficient of q^j: the set I is finite, and if sum_{s in I} m_s s <= j then for each s in I we have 0 <= m_s <= j/s. Therefore we may read off the coefficient term-by-term:
[q^j] F(q) = sum_{S subseteq I} (-1)^{|S|} * #{ (m_s)_{s in I} : sum_{s in I} m_s s + sum_{s in S}(r+s) = j }.

For each fixed S, such tuples (m_s) are in bijection with finite multisets lambda of elements of I: m_s is the multiplicity of s in lambda. Under this bijection,
wt(lambda) = sum_{s in I} m_s s.
Therefore
#{ (m_s)_{s in I} : sum_{s in I} m_s s + sum_{s in S}(r+s) = j }
= #{ lambda : wt(lambda) + sum_{s in S}(r+s) = j }.
Substituting this into the previous formula gives
[q^j] F(q) = sum_{S subseteq I} sum_{lambda : wt(lambda) + sum_{s in S}(r+s) = j} (-1)^{|S|}.
But by definition, the pairs (S, lambda) appearing in this double sum are exactly the elements of X_j. Hence
[q^j] product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)) = sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j} (-1)^{|S|},
as required.
result_payload.proof_summary: Expand each denominator factor as a geometric series and each numerator factor by choosing either 1 or -q^(r+s). The resulting terms are indexed by a subset S of I and a multiplicity tuple (m_s), equivalently by a pair (S, lambda) where lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I. The exponent is exactly wt(lambda) + sum_{s in S}(r+s), and the sign is (-1)^{|S|}. Therefore the coefficient of q^j is the signed sum over X_j.
